Relative multiplicity

Source: R/relative.multiplicity.R
relative.multiplicity.Rd

Computes relative multiplicity \(RM\) of every sample: the average, across the units present in the sample, of each unit's distance-based functional diversity \(\delta D_{\sigma}\) relative to the diversity of a reference composition of that same unit. Because every unit is compared only against itself, units that are not comparable with each other (e.g. different enzyme families) can be summarized together, and no unit dominates the index because of its size or abundance. The reference composition of every unit is built from the whole study, as set by assume_max_reference_distance and assume_homogeneous_abundance, and its diversity is computed only once.

Usage

relative.multiplicity(
  abund,
  diss,
  clust,
  sigma = 1,
  cap_at = NULL,
  average_over = "sample",
  assume_max_reference_distance = FALSE,
  assume_homogeneous_abundance = FALSE,
  chunk_size = 1e+06,
  check_large_distance_file = FALSE,
  header = TRUE
)

Arguments

abund

Numeric matrix, data.frame or sparse Matrix of abundances with samples in rows and subunits in columns. Column names are the subunit identifiers.

diss

Data frame with three columns (taken by position): the identifiers of two subunits and the distance between them, or the path to a file with them (see distance-files). Distances between every pair of subunits of the same unit must be listed, in either orientation; rows for subunits of different units are ignored, also when their distance is invalid (NA, infinite or negative). Pairs with a subunit that has zero abundance in every sample may be missing, with a warning, except with assume_homogeneous_abundance = TRUE and assume_max_reference_distance = FALSE, where every subunit counts in the reference.

clust

Vector or factor of cluster memberships: the unit of every subunit. If named, names are subunit identifiers; every column of abund must be listed, and listed subunits that are not in abund have zero abundance in every sample. Otherwise it must follow the columns of abund. A data frame is also accepted, with two columns (subunit identifiers, units) or one column of units (named by its row names, if set).

sigma

Numeric cutoff \(\sigma\) (default 1) at which two subunits are considered maximally different. Either a single value or a vector of strictly positive values with one value per unit. If named, values are matched to units by name (numeric names are matched as numbers, so "1e+05" matches the unit 100000); otherwise they follow the order of unique(clust).

cap_at

NULL (default) or a single positive number. If NULL, the ratios are not capped. Otherwise, every unit's ratio higher than cap_at is set to cap_at, e.g. cap_at = 1 for the cases where the unit is more diverse in the sample than in its reference.

average_over

The units every sample averages over, one of "sample" (default, the units present in the sample), "reference" (the units with a strictly positive reference diversity), "intersection" (the units present in the sample with a strictly positive reference diversity) or "union" (the units present in the sample or with a strictly positive reference diversity). Absent units contribute 0, and a sample without units to average over gets 0.

assume_max_reference_distance

Logical (default FALSE). If FALSE, the reference distances of a unit are the distances among all its subunits. If TRUE, every pair of subunits in the reference is at distance \(\sigma\).

assume_homogeneous_abundance

Logical (default FALSE). If FALSE, the reference abundances of a unit are those of its subunits pooled across all samples. If TRUE, all subunits of the unit have the same abundance in the reference.

chunk_size

Number of rows of a distance file read at a time (default 1e6). Lower values use less memory. Ignored when diss is in memory.

check_large_distance_file

Logical (default FALSE). If TRUE and diss is a file, the file is fully checked with check_distance_file() before computing the index: every pair of subunits of the same unit must be listed exactly once, with a valid distance. This reads the file once more and uses temporary disk space. If FALSE, only the number of rows is checked and a warning is given. Ignored when diss is in memory, which is always fully checked. See distance-files.

header

Logical (default TRUE). Whether a distance file starts with a header line (with several files, every one of them). With TRUE, a first line that looks like data (a number as third field) is an error; use FALSE for files without a header. Ignored when diss is in memory. See distance-files.

Value

Named numeric vector with the relative multiplicity \(RM\) of every sample. Samples with zero total abundance get 0.

Details

Let \(f\) be the composition of a unit in the sample, \(N_f\) its total abundance and \(\tilde{f}\) its reference composition. Then $$RM = \frac{1}{\left|\{f : N_f > 0\}\right|} \sum_{f \,:\, N_f > 0} \frac{\delta D_{\sigma}(f)}{\delta D_{\sigma}(\tilde{f})},$$ with \(\delta D_{\sigma}\) computed as in diversity.functional().

By default (average_over = "sample"), only units present in the sample are averaged: a unit with zero total abundance is ignored. In general, the average is taken over a set of units \(U\) set by average_over, $$RM = \frac{1}{|U|} \sum_{f \in U} \frac{\delta D_{\sigma}(f)}{\delta D_{\sigma}(\tilde{f})},$$ where absent units contribute 0, and \(RM = 0\) if \(U\) is empty.

Every unit that occurs in the study has a strictly positive reference diversity, so here "intersection" is the same as "sample" and "union" the same as "reference". With the pooled reference abundances (assume_homogeneous_abundance = FALSE), a unit with zero abundance across the whole study has no reference and never counts; with assume_homogeneous_abundance = TRUE, it has a reference and counts as 0 with "reference" and "union".

With assume_max_reference_distance = TRUE, the reference diversity of a unit is the inverse Simpson index of its reference abundances; if assume_homogeneous_abundance is also TRUE, it is simply the number of subunits of the unit.

Every unit's diversity depends on the distances only through the sum over its pairs of subunits \(\sum_{i<j} a_i a_j (\min(d_{ij}, \sigma) - \sigma)\), accumulated while reading the distance table. The samples and the reference are accumulated in the same read.

See also

relative.multiplicity.ref_div() when the reference diversities are already known, diversity.functional(), multiplicity.distance()

Examples

# Two units: A with subunits a1, a2, a3 and B with subunits b1, b2
clust <- c(a1 = "A", a2 = "A", a3 = "A", b1 = "B", b2 = "B")
diss <- data.frame(
  ID1 = c("a1", "a1", "a2", "b1"),
  ID2 = c("a2", "a3", "a3", "b2"),
  Distance = c(0.3, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4)
)
abund <- matrix(
  c(5, 3, 0, 2, 0,
    0, 1, 4, 2, 6,
    2, 0, 0, 0, 1),
  nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(c("S1", "S2", "S3"), names(clust))
)

relative.multiplicity(abund, diss, clust)
#>        S1        S2        S3 
#> 0.7803188 0.8759285 0.7278825 
relative.multiplicity(
  abund, diss, clust,
  assume_max_reference_distance = TRUE,
  assume_homogeneous_abundance = TRUE
)
#>        S1        S2        S3 
#> 0.4439394 0.5003883 0.4166667
